newsitem.title: USA: Search continues for victims of riverfront accident.
newsitem.headline: Search continues for victims of riverfront accident.

text.p: Rescue workers sifted through the rubble of a riverfront shopping centre on Sunday searching for missing people one day after a ship accidentally rammed the popular mall overlooking the Mississippi River.

New Orleans Mayor Marc Morial said no deaths had been confirmed after the freighter lost power and ploughed into the Riverwalk mall, destroying 15 shops and restaurants and injuring at least 116 people.
"There is no confirmed loss of life thus far and we consider that very good news under difficult circumstances," Morial said at a news conference on Sunday.
Authorities initially reported six deaths, but backed off that number late on Saturday night.
On Sunday, however, police said there were still people unaccounted for and it could take days to go through the wreckage.
"We're getting some calls from people looking for relatives or friends, but I'm not allowed to say how many or from where," a Harbour Police spokesman told Reuters.
"It will be days before searchers get through all the debris to make sure there's nobody under it," city spokeswoman Denise Estopinal told Reuters.
The Coast Guard reported that the Liberian-flagged MV Brightfield, loaded with 64,000 tonnes of corn, was headed downriver bound for Japan when it lost power, possibly because an oil pump failed.

The river pilot and crew sounded the marine emergency siren, issued radio warnings to other vessels and dropped two anchors, but could not control the ship enough to prevent the crash, a spokesman said.

As it slammed into the bank, the 735-foot (224 metre) freighter narrowly missed two docked cruise ships with 1,700 people on board and a riverboat casino packed with an estimated 800 gamblers, authorities said.

It ploughed through part of a wharf and into the mall with what witnesses called a "terrifying" sound of grinding metal and crunching concrete. Some said it felt like an earthquake, while others thought a bomb had exploded.
"I was practically running alongside the ship inside the mall when I saw it plough through the cement like a tractor ploughing dirt," said shopper Annette Angelle, of Breaux Bridge, Louisiana.
The impact wiped out 15 stores and restaurants, part of an adjacent parking garage and damaged 125 rooms in the Hilton Hotel's Riverside Wing, which towered over the mall, Estopinal said.
Many of the casualties were injured trying to flee the scene, including several who jumped from the riverboat casino to the dock when they saw the freighter coming, authorities said.
The search for victims is expected to take several more days, Estopinal said. "We're having to go very, very carefully."

The ship is partially aground against the riverbank and is believed to be supporting some portions of the collapsed mall, the Coast Guard reported. Tugs are surrounding the ship to help keep it in place while rescuers continue their search.
The Brightfield, built in Japan in 1988, is owned by the Cosco Co. of Hong Kong, operated by Clear Sky Shipping Corp., apparently a Cosco affiliate, the Coast Guard said.
New Orleans is one of the world's busiest shipping ports, with large freighters and tankers a routine sight passing by downtown and the historic French Quarter.
